digest.component_or_area: live Jira DC harness provenance test / inbound translate
propositions: The provenance test asserts a raw Jira key (RBJNAZV-1) appears in json.dumps(ticket), but the local id is lowercased to jira-rbjnazv-1 by _jira_key_to_local_id, so the case-sensitive substring match cannot pass.

The ticket payload written by the inbound create path contains no raw Jira key except as a title fallback, so it is absent whenever the issue has a summary; the DC-to-local binding lives in the binding store, which list_tickets does not return.

Because the oracle cannot distinguish a created ticket from a missing one, epic e369's headline acceptance criterion that a DC-created issue appears in the local store is unproven rather than disproven.

The fix should match the ticket by exact id equal to _jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key) and additionally assert the binding store maps that local id to the remote key, rejecting a case-insensitive substring scan.
A pure unit test should pin that _jira_key_to_local_id lowercases and prefixes the key, so the live test's id derivation is verified independently of the harness.
This is the third oracle-that-cannot-pass in the epic, caused by tests authored against an assumed output shape and hidden by earlier failures aborting the run before the assertion was reached.
